Journal

A character from the Character Builder, or just a name for one kept anywhere else.

Add:

Journals stay in this browser only (up to 30, with 400 entries each); nothing is sent anywhere. ⬇️ Export saves one to a file you can import on another device, and the Privacy page backs up every tool at once. A journal only reads its Character Builder character's name, race, class, and level; it never changes the character.

How to keep a D&D session journal

The DM keeps the campaign's notes; this is yours. Write a few lines after each session while it's fresh: what happened, who you met, what you promised, and what's still open. Next time someone asks "wait, who gave us this map?", you'll have the answer.

Five kinds of entry

  • 📖 Sessions: a numbered log with the date you played. A new one gets the next number and today's date.
  • ❗ Quests: open, done, or failed, with who gave it and the reward. Open quests sort to the top; ✅ Done marks one finished.
  • 🧑 People: who they are and whether they're friendly, neutral, or hostile toward the party.
  • 📍 Places: where it is and what you found there.
  • 💰 Loot: what it's worth, and whether it's been sold, spent, or lost.

Every entry but a session can note the session it came up in, so a search for "session 4" finds everything from that night.

Tags and search

Tag entries with anything that ties them together: a town, a villain, a faction, "owes us". Click a tag to see only those entries. Search looks through titles, notes, tags, and every field, and each word has to match.

At the table

  • Keep the journal open on a phone during the session and jot names as they come up; fill in the details afterwards.
  • Print the quests or people before a session (pick the section first; the print follows what's on screen).
  • Moving devices? ⬇️ Export the journal, then ⬆️ Import it on the other one.

Works with

Open a character's journal from the 📓 Journal button on its Character Builder sheet. Roll a past for them with the Backstory Generator, and print their abilities as Feature & Item Cards. DMs keep their side in the Worldbuilder's Campaign Notebook.
